bull_bear.body:
- Market leader in Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB) in South India
- LAB is the major product and continued to be the key contributor to the bottom line
- Uses UOP technology, described in the AR as the best and most cost-effective LAB manufacturing process, applied by more than 95 percent of all LAB manufacturers including TPL
- Captive NP production increased after adsorbent and associated hardware replacement in the NP section of the LAB plant, meeting much of the intermediate required for expanded LAB capacity
- Branded LAB offering under the Superlab brand
- Modernised caustic soda plant has enabled reduction in specific power consumption for caustic soda lye production
- CARE Ratings reaffirmed the long-term facility rating at CARE A+; Stable and the short/long-term facility at CARE A+; Stable / CARE A1+
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-product concentration in Linear Alkyl Benzene — LAB is described as the major product and the key contributor to the bottom line, and it accounted for 85.74% of turnover per the BRSR product table, so LAB pricing, spreads or an outage disproportionately drives group earnings — as seen when the LAB expansion shutdown pushed production and sales below budgeted levels.
- Import competition and dependence on trade-remedy protection — Excess global LAB capacity from Middle East and Southeast Asian additions drove rising imports into India; domestic prices were supported only marginally by the anti-dumping duty on Qatari and Iranian LAB imposed for 5 years from June 23, 2025, and by mandatory BIS certification, so any lapse or circumvention of these measures reopens price pressure. Management also cited 'pricing pressures arising from unabated imports' as adversely impacting top-line performance.
- Raw material availability and price volatility (NP, benzene, crude linkage) — NP market availability contracted significantly while prices surged as most manufacturers relied on in-house NP production, creating a supply vacuum that the Company only mitigated by importing a substantial quantity in Q3. The Indian crude oil basket rose from a USD 63-70 per barrel range to USD 113.5 per barrel in March 2026, and NP and benzene consumption ran marginally above budget.
- Geopolitical disruption of shipping and feedstock logistics — Closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-Israel war disrupted imports and, via MoPNG sector-prioritisation directives, restricted the RLNG allocation from Indian Oil Corporation during March 2026 to 80% of the contracted quantum — a direct constraint on plant energy supply.
- Structurally high Indian cost of production versus international benchmarks — The AR states that despite near-universal use of UOP technology, the cost of making LAB in India exceeds international standards due to the high cost of essential components such as energy and feedstock — a persistent margin disadvantage against imports. Power and fuel for LAB also ran above budget on unproductive consumption during the revamp shutdown and startup.
- Project execution risk on major revamps — The LAB plant shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, and the resulting lost production and sales fell below budgeted levels — evidence that turnaround slippage translates directly into volume loss.
- Propylene Oxide demand erosion from imported downstream polyols — The domestic PO market faced significant challenges from the influx of lower-priced imported downstream polyols, making PO offtake a major challenge since Q3 of FY24-25, with recovery only anticipated from Q2 of FY 26-27.
- Caustic soda oversupply and declining price trend — New domestic capacities have raised production while national capacity utilisation of the roughly 6.4 million ton aggregate capacity is around 78%, and prices are still witnessing a declining trend; caustic soda output also depends on availability of sodium chloride, whose production fluctuations affect supply and pricing.
- Carbon emission and decarbonisation-commitment exposure — The BRSR material-issues table identifies carbon emission as both risk and opportunity: the product carbon footprint influences customers' end-use emissions, industries are transitioning to cleaner energy, consumers increasingly choose low-carbon alternatives, and failing to meet decarbonization commitments can lead to reputational risks.
- Domestic-only revenue with no export diversification — The Company did not export any of its products during FY 2025-26 and exports were nil as a percentage of turnover, with sales concentrated in around 9 states, leaving earnings fully exposed to Indian demand and Indian import competition.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: TPL manufactures and sells petrochemical and industrial intermediate chemical products in India. It offers Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB), an organic compound used in the manufacture of domestic detergents, institutional and industrial cleaners, under the Superlab brand; it also produces and sells caustic soda for textile, pulp and paper, aluminium, and soap and detergent industries, and chlorine as a co-product of caustic soda. TPL additionally manufactures Propylene Oxide, sold to surfactants, specialty chemicals, propylene glycols, polyols, and fragrance and aromatics segments.

outlook.body:
- Prudent raw material sourcing and effective inventory management as a continued effort to sustain margins
- Cost optimisation, efficiency improvements and product mix enhancement alongside prudent financial management and a strong marketing strategy
- Debottlenecking and capacity expansion of the core LAB and Caustic Soda assets, with the LAB revamp (120 KTPA to 145 KTPA) and Caustic Soda modernisation (150 TPD to 250 TPD) completed in FY26
- Raising captive NP production through adsorbent and hardware replacement in the NP section of the LAB plant, to internally supply much of the intermediate needed for the expanded LAB capacity
- Pursuing a comprehensive decarbonisation roadmap — air preheater revamp, modification of the convection section of fired heaters, waste heat recovery boiler — and raising renewable power consumption
- Assessing and reducing product carbon footprint for LAB and Caustic Soda Lye to make products more environment friendly
- Sustaining profitability, improving market competitiveness and pursuing growth opportunities while maintaining financial discipline
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The planned capacity expansions in the Linear Alkyl Benzene plant and the Caustic Soda plant were completed during the last quarter of March 2026. The revamp of the LAB plant to enhance production capacity from 120 KTPA to 145 KTPA was successfully completed and commissioned in a safe manner on 11th March 2026; the shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, with production commencing in the first week of March 2026. Adsorbent and associated hardware replacement carried out in the NP section of the LAB plant facilitated an increase in captive NP production to meet much of the intermediate required for the expanded LAB capacity. The Company also successfully completed the modernisation of the Caustic Soda plant, enhancing capacity from 150 TPD to 250 TPD, with the modernised plant enabling a reduction in specific power consumption for caustic soda lye production. Under its decarbonisation roadmap, the air preheater revamp and modification of the convection section of fired heaters to enhance heat recovery from flue gas have been completed, and installation of a waste heat recovery boiler to recover heat from gas engine exhaust has been completed and is on the verge of commissioning; detailed techno-commercial evaluations are in progress for the next viable initiatives. In BRSR Section A the Company reports 3 plants and 2 offices in India and no international operations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- LAB supply remained tight globally as several facilities underwent periodic maintenance, which together with relatively stable raw material costs through the first three quarters of FY 2025-26 supported stronger domestic prices and improved margins
- Anti-dumping duty on LAB imports from Qatar and Iran for a period of 5 years, commencing 23 June 2025, marginally supported domestic LAB prices; ADD cut imports from Qatar by close to 50%
- BIS certification for LAB in the Indian market was mandated by the Indian government effective 3rd April 2023
- Closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-Israel war reduced imports and created pent-up domestic demand that the company met after commissioning its revamped LAB plant
- Global LAB market reached approximately 4.7 million tonnes in 2025 with a projected growth rate of 3.23% through 2034, potentially reaching global capacity of 6.4 million tonnes; demand fuelled by increased health consciousness and lifestyles prioritising cleanliness
- New greenfield 120 KTPA LAB plant commissioned in Saudi Arabia during the year, while a global major in Italy mothballed its 220 KTPA LAB plant citing loss of competitiveness from higher European energy costs
- Cost of making LAB in India exceeds international standards because of the high cost of essential components such as energy and feedstock
- PO offtake has been a major challenge since Q3 of FY24-25 due to the influx of lower-priced imported downstream polyols; domestic PO demand is anticipated to recover commencing from Q2 of FY 26-27
- Caustic soda prices were fairly stable during the year despite supply issues in the China market and global disruption during Q4; global caustic soda demand of approximately 84.4 million metric tons per year is projected to reach 95.9 million tons by 2034 (CAGR 1.39% over 2026-2034), with India contributing around 7%
- Indian caustic soda national capacity utilisation of aggregate capacity (approximately 6.4 million tons) is around 78%, and prices are still witnessing a declining trend as new capacities are established; textiles, alumina, inorganics, organics and paper collectively account for over 60% of the Indian market
- Crude prices: the Indian crude oil basket remained within USD 63-70 per barrel before rising sharply to USD 113.5 per barrel in March 2026 amid the Iran-Israel-US conflict
- NP sourcing was constrained as most manufacturers relied on in-house NP production, contracting market availability and surging prices

currentContext.expansion: The planned capacity expansions in the Linear Alkyl Benzene plant and the Caustic Soda plant were completed during the last quarter of March 2026. The revamp of the LAB plant to enhance production capacity from 120 KTPA to 145 KTPA was successfully completed and commissioned in a safe manner on 11th March 2026; the shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, with production commencing in the first week of March 2026. Adsorbent and associated hardware replacement carried out in the NP section of the LAB plant facilitated an increase in captive NP production to meet much of the intermediate required for the expanded LAB capacity. The Company also successfully completed the modernisation of the Caustic Soda plant, enhancing capacity from 150 TPD to 250 TPD, with the modernised plant enabling a reduction in specific power consumption for caustic soda lye production. Under its decarbonisation roadmap, the air preheater revamp and modification of the convection section of fired heaters to enhance heat recovery from flue gas have been completed, and installation of a waste heat recovery boiler to recover heat from gas engine exhaust has been completed and is on the verge of commissioning; detailed techno-commercial evaluations are in progress for the next viable initiatives. In BRSR Section A the Company reports 3 plants and 2 offices in India and no international operations.

risks.risk: Single-product concentration in Linear Alkyl Benzene
risks.note: LAB is described as the major product and the key contributor to the bottom line, and it accounted for 85.74% of turnover per the BRSR product table, so LAB pricing, spreads or an outage disproportionately drives group earnings — as seen when the LAB expansion shutdown pushed production and sales below budgeted levels.

risks.risk: Import competition and dependence on trade-remedy protection
risks.note: Excess global LAB capacity from Middle East and Southeast Asian additions drove rising imports into India; domestic prices were supported only marginally by the anti-dumping duty on Qatari and Iranian LAB imposed for 5 years from June 23, 2025, and by mandatory BIS certification, so any lapse or circumvention of these measures reopens price pressure. Management also cited 'pricing pressures arising from unabated imports' as adversely impacting top-line performance.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility (NP, benzene, crude linkage)
risks.note: NP market availability contracted significantly while prices surged as most manufacturers relied on in-house NP production, creating a supply vacuum that the Company only mitigated by importing a substantial quantity in Q3. The Indian crude oil basket rose from a USD 63-70 per barrel range to USD 113.5 per barrel in March 2026, and NP and benzene consumption ran marginally above budget.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption of shipping and feedstock logistics
risks.note: Closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-Israel war disrupted imports and, via MoPNG sector-prioritisation directives, restricted the RLNG allocation from Indian Oil Corporation during March 2026 to 80% of the contracted quantum — a direct constraint on plant energy supply.

risks.risk: Structurally high Indian cost of production versus international benchmarks
risks.note: The AR states that despite near-universal use of UOP technology, the cost of making LAB in India exceeds international standards due to the high cost of essential components such as energy and feedstock — a persistent margin disadvantage against imports. Power and fuel for LAB also ran above budget on unproductive consumption during the revamp shutdown and startup.

risks.risk: Project execution risk on major revamps
risks.note: The LAB plant shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, and the resulting lost production and sales fell below budgeted levels — evidence that turnaround slippage translates directly into volume loss.

risks.risk: Propylene Oxide demand erosion from imported downstream polyols
risks.note: The domestic PO market faced significant challenges from the influx of lower-priced imported downstream polyols, making PO offtake a major challenge since Q3 of FY24-25, with recovery only anticipated from Q2 of FY 26-27.

risks.risk: Caustic soda oversupply and declining price trend
risks.note: New domestic capacities have raised production while national capacity utilisation of the roughly 6.4 million ton aggregate capacity is around 78%, and prices are still witnessing a declining trend; caustic soda output also depends on availability of sodium chloride, whose production fluctuations affect supply and pricing.

The BRSR material-issues table identifies carbon emission as both risk and opportunity: the product carbon footprint influences customers' end-use emissions, industries are transitioning to cleaner energy, consumers increasingly choose low-carbon alternatives, and failing to meet decarbonization commitments can lead to reputational risks.

risks.risk: Domestic-only revenue with no export diversification
risks.note: The Company did not export any of its products during FY 2025-26 and exports were nil as a percentage of turnover, with sales concentrated in around 9 states, leaving earnings fully exposed to Indian demand and Indian import competition.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Tamilnadu Petroproducts Limited is a Chennai-based petrochemical and industrial-intermediate chemicals manufacturer and the market leader in Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB) in South India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: TPL manufactures and sells petrochemical and industrial intermediate chemical products in India. It offers Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB), an organic compound used in the manufacture of domestic detergents, institutional and industrial cleaners, under the Superlab brand; it also produces and sells caustic soda for textile, pulp and paper, aluminium, and soap and detergent industries, and chlorine as a co-product of caustic soda. TPL additionally manufactures Propylene Oxide, sold to surfactants, specialty chemicals, propylene glycols, polyols, and fragrance and aromatics segments.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

- **Caustic Soda / Chlorine:** Caustic soda lye, Chlorine
- **Propylene Oxide:** Propylene Oxide

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic detergents, institutional and industrial cleaners (LAB / LAS surfactants)
- Textile, pulp and paper, aluminium, and soap and detergent industries (caustic soda)
- Vinyl chloride, chlorinated paraffin wax, pulp and paper, water purification, chlorinated solvents (chlorine)
- Surfactants, specialty chemicals, propylene glycols, polyols, fragrance and aromatics (Propylene Oxide)
- India only — market leader in LAB in South India, served around 9 states during the year; no exports in FY 2025-26

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- LAB supply remained tight globally as several facilities underwent periodic maintenance, which together with relatively stable raw material costs through the first three quarters of FY 2025-26 supported stronger domestic prices and improved margins
- Anti-dumping duty on LAB imports from Qatar and Iran for a period of 5 years, commencing 23 June 2025, marginally supported domestic LAB prices; ADD cut imports from Qatar by close to 50%
- BIS certification for LAB in the Indian market was mandated by the Indian government effective 3rd April 2023
- Closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-Israel war reduced imports and created pent-up domestic demand that the company met after commissioning its revamped LAB plant
- Global LAB market reached approximately 4.7 million tonnes in 2025 with a projected growth rate of 3.23% through 2034, potentially reaching global capacity of 6.4 million tonnes; demand fuelled by increased health consciousness and lifestyles prioritising cleanliness
- New greenfield 120 KTPA LAB plant commissioned in Saudi Arabia during the year, while a global major in Italy mothballed its 220 KTPA LAB plant citing loss of competitiveness from higher European energy costs
- Cost of making LAB in India exceeds international standards because of the high cost of essential components such as energy and feedstock
- PO offtake has been a major challenge since Q3 of FY24-25 due to the influx of lower-priced imported downstream polyols; domestic PO demand is anticipated to recover commencing from Q2 of FY 26-27
- Caustic soda prices were fairly stable during the year despite supply issues in the China market and global disruption during Q4; global caustic soda demand of approximately 84.4 million metric tons per year is projected to reach 95.9 million tons by 2034 (CAGR 1.39% over 2026-2034), with India contributing around 7%
- Indian caustic soda national capacity utilisation of aggregate capacity (approximately 6.4 million tons) is around 78%, and prices are still witnessing a declining trend as new capacities are established; textiles, alumina, inorganics, organics and paper collectively account for over 60% of the Indian market
- Crude prices: the Indian crude oil basket remained within USD 63-70 per barrel before rising sharply to USD 113.5 per barrel in March 2026 amid the Iran-Israel-US conflict
- NP sourcing was constrained as most manufacturers relied on in-house NP production, contracting market availability and surging prices

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Prudent raw material sourcing and effective inventory management as a continued effort to sustain margins
- Cost optimisation, efficiency improvements and product mix enhancement alongside prudent financial management and a strong marketing strategy
- Debottlenecking and capacity expansion of the core LAB and Caustic Soda assets, with the LAB revamp (120 KTPA to 145 KTPA) and Caustic Soda modernisation (150 TPD to 250 TPD) completed in FY26
- Raising captive NP production through adsorbent and hardware replacement in the NP section of the LAB plant, to internally supply much of the intermediate needed for the expanded LAB capacity
- Pursuing a comprehensive decarbonisation roadmap — air preheater revamp, modification of the convection section of fired heaters, waste heat recovery boiler — and raising renewable power consumption
- Assessing and reducing product carbon footprint for LAB and Caustic Soda Lye to make products more environment friendly
- Sustaining profitability, improving market competitiveness and pursuing growth opportunities while maintaining financial discipline

capex_expansion.body: The planned capacity expansions in the Linear Alkyl Benzene plant and the Caustic Soda plant were completed during the last quarter of March 2026. The Company also successfully completed the modernisation of the Caustic Soda plant, enhancing capacity from 150 TPD to 250 TPD, with the modernised plant enabling a reduction in specific power consumption for caustic soda lye production. Under its decarbonisation roadmap, the air preheater revamp and modification of the convection section of fired heaters to enhance heat recovery from flue gas have been completed, and installation of a waste heat recovery boiler to recover heat from gas engine exhaust has been completed and is on the verge of commissioning; detailed techno-commercial evaluations are in progress for the next viable initiatives.
